family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Split text on newline characters. Leave the first line unchanged, but prepend n spaces to every subsequent line, including empty ones. Rejoin the lines with newline characters.
hidden_tests: assert indent_except_first('keep first as is\nindent this one', 6) == 'keep first as is\n      indent this one'
assert indent_except_first('no change needed', 0) == 'no change needed'
assert indent_except_first('first line stays\n  already indented', 2) == 'first line stays\n    already indented'

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: For each line of text (split on newline), if the line begins with a single tab character, replace just that leading tab with four spaces, leaving the rest of the line untouched. Lines that do not start with a tab are returned unchanged.
visible_tests: assert dedent_tabs('no tab here') == 'no tab here'
hidden_tests: assert dedent_tabs('  spaces not tab') == '  spaces not tab'
assert dedent_tabs('\n\ttab after blank') == '\n    tab after blank'

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a list of strings, prepend n spaces to each one and join the resulting strings with newline characters into a single string. An empty list of lines produces an empty string.
hidden_tests:
assert indent_block(['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'], 1) == ' a
 b
 c
 d'
assert indent_block(['multi word line here'], 4) == '    multi word line here'
reference:
def indent_block(lines, n):
    return "\n".join(" " * n + line for line in lines)

spec: For every line of text (split on newline) that starts with at least old_n leading space characters, remove the first old_n spaces and put new_n spaces in their place. Lines with fewer than old_n leading spaces are left completely unchanged. Rejoin the lines with newline characters.
visible_tests: assert reindent('    a\n    b', 4, 2) == '  a\n  b'

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a list of item strings and a bullet marker string, render one line per item as the bullet followed by a space and the item text, joined together with newline characters. An empty list of items produces an empty string.
hidden_tests:
assert render_bullets(['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'], '+') == '+ a
+ b
+ c
+ d'

assert render_bullets(['milk', 'eggs', 'bread', 'butter'], '-') == '- milk
- eggs
- bread
- butter'
assert render_bullets(['item with spaces'], '*') == '* item with spaces'
assert render_bullets(['long item text here', 'short'], '-') == '- long item text here\n- short'

assert render_bullets(['first', 'second', 'third', 'fourth', 'fifth'], '*') == '* first
* second
* third
* fourth
* fifth'
assert render_bullets(['single bullet item'], '-') == '- single bullet item'
reference:
def render_bullets(items, bullet):
    return "\n".join(bullet + " " + item for item in items)

3. blue

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a list of (level, text) pairs where level is a non-negative integer nesting depth, render one line per pair: two spaces per level of indentation, then a dash, a space, and the text. Join the lines with newline characters. An empty list of items produces an empty string.
hidden_tests: assert render_nested_bullets([(1, 'no top level')]) == '  - no top level'

assert render_nested_bullets([(0, 'root'), (1, 'child1'), (1, 'child2'), (2, 'grandchild')]) == '- root
  - child1
  - child2
    - grandchild'
assert render_nested_bullets([(0, 'a'), (2, 'skip level')]) == '- a\n    - skip level'
assert render_nested_bullets([(0, 'item with spaces')]) == '- item with spaces'

assert render_nested_bullets([(0, 'top1'), (1, 'mid1'), (2, 'low1'), (0, 'top2')]) == '- top1
  - mid1
    - low1
- top2'

assert render_nested_bullets([(0, 'z'), (1, 'y'), (2, 'x'), (3, 'w')]) == '- z
  - y
    - x
      - w'
reference:
def render_nested_bullets(items):
    return "\n".join("  " * level + "- " + text for level, text in items)

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a list of (text, done) pairs where done is a boolean, render one line per pair: '[x] ' followed by the text if done is True, otherwise '[ ] ' followed by the text. Join the lines with newline characters. An empty list produces an empty string.
visible_tests: assert render_checklist([('buy milk', False), ('clean', True)]) == '[ ] buy milk\n[x] clean'
assert render_checklist([('done task', True)]) == '[x] done task'
hidden_tests: assert render_checklist([('a', True), ('b', False), ('c', True)]) == '[x] a\n[ ] b\n[x] c'
assert render_checklist([('only undone', False)]) == '[ ] only undone'
assert render_checklist([('x', True), ('y', True)]) == '[x] x\n[x] y'
assert render_checklist([('p', False), ('q', False)]) == '[ ] p\n[ ] q'
assert render_checklist([('task with spaces', True)]) == '[x] task with spaces'

assert render_checklist([('1', False), ('2', True), ('3', False), ('4', True)]) == '[ ] 1
[x] 2
[ ] 3
[x] 4'

assert render_checklist([('a', False), ('b', True), ('c', False), ('d', True), ('e', False)]) == '[ ] a
[x] b
[ ] c
[x] d
[ ] e'
assert render_checklist([('empty text', True), ('', False)]) == '[x] empty text\n[ ] '
assert render_checklist([('first', True), ('second', False)]) == '[x] first\n[ ] second'
assert render_checklist([('all done', True), ('also done', True)]) == '[x] all done\n[x] also done'
assert render_checklist([('none done', False), ('still none', False)]) == '[ ] none done\n[ ] still none'
reference:
def render_checklist(items):
    return "\n".join(("[x] " if done else "[ ] ") + text for text, done in items)

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a list of item strings, a bullet marker string, and an indent width, render one line per item as indent spaces, then the bullet, a space, then the item text. Join the lines with newline characters. An empty list of items produces an empty string.
hidden_tests: assert render_bullets_indented(['item with spaces'], '*', 5) == '     * item with spaces'

reference:
def render_bullets_indented(items, bullet, indent):
    return "\n".join(" " * indent + bullet + " " + item for item in items)

visible_tests: assert render_definition_list([('cat', 'an animal'), ('run', 'to move fast')]) == 'cat: an animal\nrun: to move fast'
hidden_tests: assert render_definition_list([('term with spaces', 'a longer definition here')]) == 'term with spaces: a longer definition here'

assert render_definition_list([('k1', 'v1'), ('k2', 'v2'), ('k3', 'v3'), ('k4', 'v4')]) == 'k1: v1
k2: v2
k3: v3
k4: v4'

assert render_definition_list([('a', 'b'), ('c', 'd'), ('e', 'f'), ('g', 'h')]) == 'a: b
c: d
e: f
g: h'

def render_definition_list(pairs):
    return "\n".join(f"{term}: {definition}" for term, definition in pairs)

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a digit string and a count keep, mask every character except the last keep characters, replacing masked characters with '*' and keeping the total length unchanged. If keep is zero or negative, mask the whole string; if keep is greater than or equal to the string's length, return the string unchanged.

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a digit string, keep the first 3 and last 2 characters visible and replace everything in between with '*' characters, preserving the total length. If the string has 5 or fewer characters, mask the entire string.

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given an international phone number string formatted as '+CC-AAA-BBB-CCCC' (dash-separated segments), keep the leading country-code segment and the final segment unchanged, and replace every segment in between with asterisk characters of the same length as that segment.

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a digit string and a single mask character ch, replace all but the last 4 characters with ch, keeping the last 4 characters visible and the total length unchanged. If the string has 4 or fewer characters, return it unchanged.

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a dash-formatted phone number string, optionally followed by a space, the letter 'x', and an extension number (for example '123-456-7890 x123'), mask all digits of the phone number except the last 4 with '*', keeping the dashes in their original positions. Any extension suffix is left fully visible and unchanged; if there is no extension, none is added.

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a digit string and two counts keep_first and keep_last, keep that many characters visible at the start and end of the string respectively and mask everything in between with '*', preserving the total length. If keep_first plus keep_last is greater than or equal to the string's length, return the string unchanged.
